# Adjust Kinships

## Overview

When performing heritability estimation using [Haseman-Elston](http://dougspeed.com/haseman-elston-regression/) or [PCGC Regression](http://dougspeed.com/pcgc-regression/) with covariates included, adjusted kinship matrices must be created first. These are generated by regressing original kinship matrices against the covariates.

The key distinction: REML jointly regresses phenotypes on both covariates and kinships, whereas HE and PCGC regression use adjusted phenotypes with adjusted kinships. You need not separately adjust phenotypes, as this step is handled within the HE and PCGC routines.

**Important:** Always review the screen output, which provides argument suggestions and memory usage estimates.

---

## Main Arguments

The primary command is `--adjust-grm <outfile>`.

### Required Options

- `--grm <kinfile>` — specifies the kinship matrix. If using multiple kinship matrices for HE or PCGC regression, adjust each separately.
- `--covar <covarfile>` — provides covariates in [PLINK format](http://dougspeed.com/phenotypes-and-covariates/)

### Optional Filtering

For HE or PCGC regression on sample subsets, apply equivalent filtering here using:
- `--keep <keepfile>` — to specify particular samples
- `--pheno <phenofile>` — to include only samples with valid phenotypes

The adjusted kinship matrix output uses the stem `<outfile>` (see [Kinship Formats](http://dougspeed.com/kinship-formats/) for storage details).

---

## Example

Using covariates from [Test Datasets](http://dougspeed.com/test-datasets/) and kinships from [Calculate Kinships](http://dougspeed.com/calculate-kinships/):

```
./ldak.out --adjust-grm HumDef.covar --grm HumDef --covar human.covar
```

Adjusted kinships are saved with stem `HumDef.covar`.
